findings.claim: The proposed lock protocol admits deadlock between an intake and existing multi-statement writers, and between two existing writers, because statement-level AFTER guards take the head exclusive lock mid-transaction while the intake holds source-row share locks from the referral preflight.
findings.evidence: scope:172-174 orders intake as epoch read -> preflight that locks source rows -> head shared lock; Postgres row locks persist to transaction end, so the intake waits on the head while holding FOR SHARE on partners/links (supabase/candidates/20260904_research_partner_referral_v1.sql@ac36e60:541, :555-558). scope:179-181 has writers take the head exclusive lock in statement guards; research_referral_v1_execute (same file ~:717 insert partner_links, ~:722-725 FOR UPDATE+update links, ~:746 insert attribution_touches, ~:674/:711 FOR SHARE of partners,members, ~:817 insert transfer events) is multi-statement across guarded relations, so after its first guarded statement it holds head X and may then wait on a row the intake share-locks -> cycle. Two such writers can likewise cycle (head X vs each other's row locks), a regression for writers that never conflicted before. scope:208 concedes 'not a demonstrated deadlock-freedom'.
findings.fix: Amend the packet before drafting the guard SQL: the intake must hold no source-row lock while requesting or holding the head lock. Either (a) run the canonical locking preflight in a separately committed transaction, bind its result to the observed epoch, and refuse after taking the head shared lock if the epoch moved (the guards already advance the epoch on every write to those relations, so the epoch is the serialization token), or (b) take the head shared lock before any preflight and make writer guards BEFORE ... FOR EACH STATEMENT so both sides acquire head then rows; in both cases record that writer-vs-writer serialization through the head is intended and bounded. State the chosen order as an explicit invariant the verifier's 'every listed writer competing before/after the head boundary' case (:256-257) must exercise.
